[cols="2h,5,5,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Curve |`secp256k1` |`ed25519` |`x25519` |`p256`

|What it does
|BIP 340 Schnorr and ECDSA signatures, recoverable signatures, ECDH in three forms, tweaks, ElligatorSwift, MuSig2, silent payments, SPKI and PKCS#8
|Ed25519 signatures, and Ed25519ph over SHA-512 for a message given in pieces; the X25519 secret key of a key pair
|Key agreement (Diffie-Hellman on Curve25519): two parties who exchanged public keys share a 32-byte secret; `kx_keypair`, libsodium's `crypto_kx`, gives a client and a server a session key for each direction
|Key pairs made from a 32-byte scalar or drawn from `random_device`, public keys validated once, as SEC 1's uncompressed point or two coordinates, ECDSA over a SHA-256 digest with RFC 6979's nonce, raw and DER, and low S checked or normalized, ECDH's raw x coordinate, SPKI and PKCS#8

|Security level
|about 128 bits (link:https://www.secg.org/sec2-v2.pdf[SEC 2, Recommended Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters])
|about 128 bits (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032[RFC 8032, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)])
|about 128 bits (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7748[RFC 7748, Elliptic Curves for Security (X25519 and X448)])
|about 128 bits (link:https://www.secg.org/sec2-v2.pdf[SEC 2, Recommended Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters])

|Key sizes
|secret 32 bytes; public 33 bytes compressed, 65 bytes uncompressed (link:https://www.secg.org/sec1-v2.pdf[SEC 1 version 2, Elliptic Curve Cryptography, sections 2.3.3 and 2.3.4: a point's encodings]), 32 bytes x-only, 64 bytes as ElligatorSwift (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0324.mediawiki[BIP 324, version 2 P2P encrypted transport protocol]); SPKI 56 or 88 bytes (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5480[RFC 5480, Elliptic Curve Cryptography Subject Public Key Information]), PKCS#8 135 bytes (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5208[RFC 5208, PKCS #8: Private-Key Information Syntax], link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5915[RFC 5915, Elliptic Curve Private Key Structure])
|secret 32 bytes (the seed); public 32 bytes
|secret 32 bytes; public 32 bytes
|secret 32 bytes (the scalar); public 65 bytes uncompressed (link:https://www.secg.org/sec1-v2.pdf[SEC 1 version 2, Elliptic Curve Cryptography, sections 2.3.3 and 2.3.4: a point's encodings]); SPKI 91 bytes (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5480[RFC 5480, Elliptic Curve Cryptography Subject Public Key Information]), PKCS#8 138 bytes (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5208[RFC 5208, PKCS #8: Private-Key Information Syntax], link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5915[RFC 5915, Elliptic Curve Private Key Structure])

|Signature sizes
|64 bytes, MuSig2's aggregate too (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki[BIP 327, MuSig2 for BIP340-compatible multi-signatures]); 65 bytes recoverable; ECDSA in DER up to 72
|64 bytes
|none: no signatures
|ECDSA: 64 bytes, r and s (link:https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1363/2049/[IEEE 1363-2000, Standard Specifications for Public-Key Cryptography: a signature as the two integers r and s, each at the order's length]); in DER up to 72 (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3279#section-2.2.3[RFC 3279, section 2.2.3: an ECDSA signature in X.509, the DER of a SEQUENCE of the INTEGERs r and s])

|Speed
|BIP340 signature of a 32-byte message: native, libsecp256k1 11.8 µs; wasip2, libsecp256k1 68.7 µs; wasip3, libsecp256k1 77.6 µs; emscripten, libsecp256k1 69.2 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)
|signature of a 32-byte message: native, libsodium 11.8 µs; wasip2, libsodium 22.8 µs; wasip3, libsodium 26.4 µs; emscripten, libsodium 21.5 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)
|agreement of a secret key and a public key: native, libsodium 22.4 µs; wasip2, libsodium 58.1 µs; wasip3, libsodium 58.4 µs; emscripten, libsodium 54.7 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)
|ECDSA signature of a 32-byte SHA-256 digest: native, BearSSL 162 µs; wasip2, BearSSL 243 µs; wasip3, BearSSL 280 µs; emscripten, BearSSL 214 µs; ECDSA verification of a 32-byte SHA-256 digest: native, BearSSL 272 µs; wasip2, BearSSL 483 µs; wasip3, BearSSL 508 µs; emscripten, BearSSL 486 µs; x coordinate of the ECDH shared point with a peer's public key: native, BearSSL 136 µs; wasip2, BearSSL 244 µs; wasip3, BearSSL 262 µs; emscripten, BearSSL 250 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)

|Constant time, measured
|libsecp256k1: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux; libsecp256k1's own `+ctime_tests.c+`, and webcpp's code around it: the key pair's making, its signatures and x-only tweak, ECDH in three forms, the secret key's tweaks and negation, and PKCS#8), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang; the same paths as memcheck's) and dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts; `+ecdh_x+`), nothing found; wasip2, dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts; `+ecdh_x+`), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)
|libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; wasip2, dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)
|libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found, and dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts): nothing found with arm64's DIT (data-independent timing) bit set, which webcpp sets around every call on 64-bit ARM under macOS, iOS, Linux and Android where the CPU has it, as Apple requires of constant-time code (link:https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations[Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations]); the lane's dudect sets nothing itself and measures what a program gets: \|t\| 1.8 to 2.8 against the threshold 10 (2026-11-21, five runs), while its `dudect_planted`, an early-exit scan of the secret key run inside the same guard, reads \|t\| 66.72 and 65.53 (2026-11-21): DIT does not hide a leak. Without DIT, dudect times `agree` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at \|t\| 6.7 to 14.5 (2026-11-19) and 4.3 to 7.8 (2026-11-21, three runs): about one nanosecond in 15 µs. Each on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build. libsodium does not set DIT, and webcpp sets nothing on x86, WebAssembly or Windows on ARM64; wasip2, dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts): an open finding, its cause measured: dudect times `agree` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at \|t\| 13 to 32 (2026-11-18; a fixed key against another fixed key: 22.9) and 107 to 260 (2026-11-19), and 25.25 in the lane on 2026-11-21, against the threshold 10, under wasmtime 47 on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build. The cause is Apple silicon's DIT (data-independent timing), which wasmtime does not set (link:https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations[Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations]): with DIT set in wasmtime's main thread, an experiment and not the lane, the same case reads \|t\| 1.5 to 2.1; no branch on a secret was found in the WebAssembly or in wasmtime's compiled code. The lane cannot set DIT from inside the WebAssembly, so it prints this value on wasip2 without judging it; the CI's x86-64 run measures it next; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)
|BearSSL: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux; the key pair's making, `+sign_ecdsa+` then `+normalize_ecdsa+` and `+check_low_s+` on the fresh signature, `+ecdh_x+` and `+decode_pkcs8+`; BearSSL's own branches on its signing's verdicts listed in `+bearssl_verdicts.supp+`; nothing found with webcpp's fix to BearSSL's decoding of the nonce, whose leak of the nonce's bit length this checker found on 2026-11-21 (Valgrind 3.22, arm64 Linux)), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang; the same paths as memcheck's; found the same leak, nothing after the fix (clang 18, arm64 Linux, 2026-11-21)) and dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts; `+sign_ecdsa+` and `+ecdh_x+`, each against the key pair's scalar), nothing found; wasip2, dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts; `+sign_ecdsa+` and `+ecdh_x+`, each against the key pair's scalar), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)

|Standards
|link:https://www.secg.org/sec2-v2.pdf[SEC 2, Recommended Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters], link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340.mediawiki[BIP 340, Schnorr signatures for secp256k1], link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6979[RFC 6979, deterministic ECDSA nonces], link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0324.mediawiki[BIP 324, version 2 P2P encrypted transport protocol], link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki[BIP 327, MuSig2 for BIP340-compatible multi-signatures], link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0352.mediawiki[BIP 352, Silent Payments]
|link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032[RFC 8032, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)], link:https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final[FIPS 186-5, the Digital Signature Standard]
|link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7748[RFC 7748, Elliptic Curves for Security (X25519 and X448)]
|link:https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final[FIPS 186-5, the Digital Signature Standard], link:https://www.secg.org/sec2-v2.pdf[SEC 2, Recommended Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters], link:https://www.secg.org/sec1-v2.pdf[SEC 1 version 2, Elliptic Curve Cryptography, sections 2.3.3 and 2.3.4: a point's encodings], link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6979[RFC 6979, deterministic ECDSA nonces]

|Ecosystems that require it
|Bitcoin (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0340.mediawiki[BIP 340, Schnorr signatures for secp256k1]), Ethereum (link:https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf[The Ethereum yellow paper, appendix F: ECDSA on secp256k1]), Nostr (link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md[Nostr NIP-01, events signed with BIP 340 on secp256k1])
|SSH keys (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8709[RFC 8709, Ed25519 and Ed448 public keys for SSH]), Signal's signatures on its Curve25519 keys (link:https://signal.org/docs/specifications/xeddsa/[Signal, the XEdDSA and VXEdDSA signature schemes]), Tor's identity keys (link:https://spec.torproject.org/cert-spec.html[Tor's specifications, Ed25519 certificates]), Solana's accounts (link:https://solana.com/docs/core/accounts[Solana's documentation, accounts and their Ed25519 keys])
|TLS 1.3 (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-4.2.7[RFC 8446, TLS 1.3, section 4.2.7 (supported groups)]), SSH (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8731[RFC 8731, Secure Shell key exchange with Curve25519]), WireGuard (link:https://www.wireguard.com/protocol/[WireGuard's protocol, cryptography]), Signal (link:https://signal.org/docs/specifications/x3dh/[Signal, the X3DH key agreement protocol])
|passkeys' ES256 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/#sctn-alg-identifier[W3C Web Authentication, its algorithm identifiers: ES256 is ECDSA on P-256 with SHA-256]), TLS 1.3 (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-4.2.7[RFC 8446, TLS 1.3, section 4.2.7 (supported groups)])

|Browsers' WebCrypto
|no: WebCrypto offers P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519 and X25519, not secp256k1 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|yes: Ed25519 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|yes: X25519 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|yes: P-256, for ECDSA and ECDH (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])

|Choose it for compatibility with
|Bitcoin's keys and signatures; Nostr's event signatures (link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md[Nostr NIP-01, events signed with BIP 340 on secp256k1]); Ethereum's ECDSA verification with a known key; ECDH in the raw x-coordinate form of Nostr's encrypted messages (link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/44.md[Nostr NIP-44, encrypted payloads]); Ethereum's recoverable signatures and uncompressed keys (link:https://ethereum.github.io/yellowpaper/paper.pdf[The Ethereum yellow paper, appendix F: ECDSA on secp256k1]), the address hashing being a domain library's; BIP 32's tweaks of the full key, its derivation of the tweak being a domain library's (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0032.mediawiki[BIP 32, hierarchical deterministic wallets]); keys exchanged with OpenSSL as SPKI or PKCS#8 (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5480[RFC 5480, Elliptic Curve Cryptography Subject Public Key Information], link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5915[RFC 5915, Elliptic Curve Private Key Structure]), in DER or PEM (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7468[RFC 7468, textual encodings of PKIX, PKCS and CMS structures (PEM)]); Bitcoin's version 2 transport, whose keys are ElligatorSwift encodings (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0324.mediawiki[BIP 324, version 2 P2P encrypted transport protocol]); MuSig2's multisignatures (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0327.mediawiki[BIP 327, MuSig2 for BIP340-compatible multi-signatures]); silent payments (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0352.mediawiki[BIP 352, Silent Payments]), the addresses and transactions being a domain library's
|SSH, Tor and Solana keys and signatures, and any protocol that names RFC 8032's Ed25519 or Ed25519ph; verification is strict (libsodium's rules), which some lenient verifiers are not. Not Bitcoin, Ethereum or Nostr, whose keys are secp256k1's
|TLS 1.3's and SSH's key exchange, WireGuard, Signal; libsodium's `crypto_box` keys, and the session keys of `crypto_kx` with `kx_keypair` (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/key_exchange[libsodium's documentation, key exchange]). The Ed25519 public key of a peer converts with `curves::ed25519::to_x25519_public`. A shared secret goes through a KDF before it keys a cipher. Every case of Wycheproof's X25519 file is tested (link:https://github.com/C2SP/wycheproof[Project Wycheproof, test vectors for cryptographic libraries])
|Browsers' WebCrypto, whose raw export of a P-256 public key is the uncompressed point `public_key::make` takes (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API]) and whose ECDH `deriveBits` is the raw x `ecdh_x` gives (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/#ecdh-operations[W3C Web Cryptography API, ECDH's deriveBits: the shared point's x coordinate, its first length bits]); passkeys and TLS. Not Bitcoin, Ethereum or Nostr, whose keys are secp256k1's
|===
